name: String of Firecrackers
description: A braid of red paper crackers on a long fuse. Light it, walk away, and for a few seconds somewhere else sounds exactly like a gunfight.

name: Air Horn
description: A canister with a plastic trumpet screwed to the top. There is no fuse and no cleverness: it starts the moment you set it down, and it is as loud as a man screaming.

name: Wind-Up Alarm Clock
description: A brass twin-bell clock off somebody's bedside table. Wind it, set it, leave it in a house on the other side of the district and be somewhere else when it decides to go off.

name: Transistor Radio
description: A pocket radio tuned to a station that stopped broadcasting. It hisses cheerfully to nobody for an hour at a time, which is longer than most plans need.

name: Salvaged Car Alarm
description: A siren box cut out of a hatchback with its wiring loom still attached, taped to a motorcycle battery. It wails like the car it came out of.

name: Hand-Crank Siren
description: A civil defence siren on a tripod, wound up by hand until the rotor is screaming and then let go. It carries further than anything else you can pick up.

name: Wind Bell
description: A heavy iron bell on a bracket, hung so the weather rings it. Quiet as these things go, and it keeps at it for most of an afternoon.

name: Quarry Blasting Cap
description: A detonator and a stick of quarry charge on a mechanical timer, lifted from a site store. It is the loudest thing anybody will ever hear you do, and it is over before you can regret it.
